headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: MinerU can use MCP and concurrent sessions while awesome-python is non-runnable, so most other pairwise harms are blocked or minimal.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection bridge is documented. agent_a is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while agent_b can use MCP but only exposes document inputs and allowlisted egress; there is no shared channel or evidence that B ingests A’s outputs by default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts or MCP inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy-paste of untrusted text into agent_b.
Require provenance labels on any imported content.
Use a read-only handoff file with explicit delimiters.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before MCP ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and is non-runnable, while agent_b processes local documents and has allowlisted egress. With no shared workspace or secrets handling shown, leakage is not a default pathway; the remaining risk is limited to unusual operator-created sharing.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local files, agent_b may process content originating from agent_a’s workspace.
IF operator places sensitive documents into agent_b inputs, those contents can flow through its inference/backend path.
mitigations: Use separate input directories.
Do not co-locate sensitive files with shared artifacts.
Review allowlisted destinations for agent_b.
Delete temporary document outputs after use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b supports multi-threaded concurrent inference and multiple instances, but it cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. agent_a is non-runnable and has no write or concurrency surface, so direct write-write conflict is mostly absent; only limited contention via shared orchestration remains.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable resource, contention can occur.
IF agent_b is wrapped with additional write permissions outside the profile, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Run each agent in its own session.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Serialize access in the orchestrator.
Monitor for duplicate processing of the same document.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a collection repo and not runnable, so it cannot generate operational facts for agent_b to act on by default. agent_b processes documents but has no downstream action authority shown; therefore cascading error is limited unless an operator manually treats A’s content as authoritative input.
conditions: IF operator feeds agent_a-derived text into agent_b as authoritative instructions, B may propagate errors.
IF agent_b is later connected to an action-taking toolchain, downstream impact increases.
mitigations: Require human verification of imported content.
Separate extraction from decision-making steps.
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted reference material.
Add a review checkpoint before any downstream use.
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance checks in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. agent_a has no data classes or runnable processing, and agent_b’s profile shows no secrets handled, no OAuth scopes, and offline/private isolation; there is no documented residency, retention, or regulated-data pathway to compare.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into agent_b inputs, a compliance review is required.
IF deployment changes residency or retention settings, the assessment must be revisited.
mitigations: Confirm no regulated data is routed to either agent.
Document retention settings for agent_b.
Keep agent_a as a reference-only repository.
Review deployment region and storage policy.
requires-engineering: add formal data-class handling controls.
